one_line: Nana Sahib’s worldly secretary and rebel pamphleteer moving through Kanpur, London and Constantinople on the eve of 1857.

appearance.age_look: late 20s to early 30s, lean and wiry, with the alert build of a fast-moving clerk turned conspirator
appearance.face: oval face with sharp cheekbones, medium brown North Indian complexion, straight nose, neatly groomed medium-thickness moustache, intelligent narrow eyes with a steady analytical gaze, default expression calm and observant with a hint of wry determination
appearance.hair: straight, black hair kept relatively short at the back, brushed back from the forehead with a slight wave; a deep maroon, neatly tied small pagri (turban) in mid-19th-century North Indian style, with a thin gold trim along its edge and a modest central knot but no oversized ornament
appearance.costume: A mid-19th-century North Indian noble secretary’s attire: long cream-coloured cotton angarkha (overlapping front robe) reaching just below the knees, with a subtle vertical weave and a slightly flared skirt, fastened on the right side with small cloth ties; over it, a fitted deep navy-blue woollen chapkan-style coat without excessive embroidery, hem and cuffs edged by a narrow maroon piping; plain off-white churidar trousers closely gathered at the ankles; a simple dark brown leather kamarband (waist belt) wrapping twice around his waist; feet in brown leather mojari shoes with slightly upturned toes, minimally decorated; he wears a light cotton shawl in muted grey-blue draped from his left shoulder, practical for travel; modest jewellery limited to a small silver signet ring on his right hand and a thin steel kara-style bangle on his left wrist, reflecting a restrained, educated elite rather than ostentatious court dress.
appearance.signature: A compact, mid-19th-century French-style tabletop printing press rendered as a portable prop: dark iron frame with a flat wooden platen, a single sturdy lever and a few loose metal type blocks and rolled paper sheets held in his left arm, symbolising his role in rebel print culture rather than battlefield combat.

ref_desc: Azimullah Khan has an oval medium-brown face with a neat moustache, short black hair under a maroon pagri, cream angarkha, navy chapkan, off-white churidar, brown mojari, grey-blue shawl, and carries a compact dark-iron printing press with papers.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Azimullah Khan: a lean late-twenties North Indian man with an oval medium-brown face, sharp cheekbones, straight nose, intelligent narrow eyes and a neatly groomed moustache, his short black hair brushed back beneath a deep maroon mid-19th-century pagri. He wears a cream cotton angarkha falling just below the knees, overlapping and tied on the right, over which sits a fitted navy-blue chapkan coat edged in maroon piping at cuffs and hem, paired with off-white churidar trousers and brown leather mojari shoes. A muted grey-blue cotton shawl is draped from his left shoulder and wrapped lightly around his back, and he has a small silver signet ring on his right hand and a thin steel bangle on his left wrist. In his arms he carries a compact dark-iron French-style printing press prop with a wooden platen, single lever, scattered metal type blocks and rolled paper sheets. Show him from multiple angles in consistent colours, emphasising his calm, observant expression and dignified, historically grounded 1850s attire.
